title: Pool Surge Sculptor — compact dashboard & burst controls
creator: Lena Park
description: Design a compact, single-pane control and health surface for Dedicated GPU pools that surfaces surge/burst settings, immediate health indicators, and cost/latency tradeoffs. Target audience: platform engineers and on-call SREs who need a lightweight operational view during incidents and an easy-to-use surface for configuring autoscale and burst policies without leaving the pool details page. Deliverables: responsive Figma prototype (desktop + narrow tablet), interaction spec for autoscale policy composer, and handoff tokens for engineering. The visual language should be compact and scannable: summary row, short-form KPIs, sparklines, toggleable advanced controls, and inline preview of estimated cost delta for burst changes.
acceptance_criteria: Single-pane prototype that fits within the existing pool details column width (max 920px) and degrades gracefully to 320px width for narrow consoles
Health summary row with color-coded status (OK, Degraded, Critical) and fast-path links to logs and trace views
Autoscale composer allowing target concurrency and cost-budget inputs with live estimate preview
Burst tuning slider and quick-presets (none, small, medium, aggressive) with ability to set cooldown and duration
Design tokens and spacing documented for engineering handoff, plus redlines for accessible color contrast
Prototype demonstrates interactions for applying a policy, canary-ing to 10% of traffic, and rollback
Handoff includes a single example of telemetry points to emit (e.g., burst_applied, autoscale_policy_updated)
UX copy is finalized and reviewed by PM and SRE (no placeholder text)
design_notes: Prioritized a compact summary row over a full-width timeline to keep the surface usable in sidebars and nested panes
Chose discrete presets for burst to reduce decision friction; advanced mode exposes sliders and per-GPU caps
Cost estimate is intentionally conservative: shows 95th percentile token cost delta and peak GPU-hours instead of mean to avoid surprises
Decided against live streaming of per-request traces in this surface to keep initial implementation lightweight; deep links to trace explorer included
Animations should be subtle: single easing on KPI transitions and no motion for critical status changes to ensure readability during incidents
accessibility: Color contrast meets WCAG AA for all status states; color + icon used for status to avoid color-only dependence
All controls reachable via keyboard; slider has a text-entry fallback; ARIA labels included in spec
Tooltips avoid hover-only explanations; long-form help panel available via a persistent help icon
Focus states specified in handoff tokens for devs (outline thickness, color, and offset)
interactions: Apply policy flow: edit -> preview estimate -> dry-run (optional) -> canary to 10% -> monitor -> promote/rollback
Burst quick-presets apply immediately but show a dismissible banner with undo for 30s
Changing cooldown or duration updates the estimated cost and expected latency improvement in real-time
Health status updates are pushed to the UI via websocket; a visual pulse indicates fresh data within the last 10s
When pool is critical, controls are locked with clear rationale and a CTA to create an incident and request emergency capacity
